title: How to Install a Utility Sink: Drain, Vent, and Water Supply Integration

locations.name: Basement utility area (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript references being in a basement with a washer/dryer nearby; vent/drain layout discussed as if in a basement utility space

summary: This This Old House episode demonstrates installing a utility sink in a basement-style laundry area by modifying an existing washer drain and vent to accommodate a new sink drain. The tutorial covers evaluating the standpipe/drain layout, reducing and reconfiguring piping with 45° elbows to align drains, dry-fitting before glue, and using a slip/repair coupling for final connections. It also shows replacing an aging washing-machine shut-off valve, rerouting hot and cold supply lines to the sink, and installing a faucet with a pull-out spray. The workflow emphasizes venting considerations, accurate marks for reassembly, careful deburring and cleaning of PVC joints, glue application, leak testing with water, and verifying both hot and cold water supply during the final test.

sections.title: Drain and vent planning in a basement utility area
concepts: vent prevents drain gurgling by breaking vacuum
sections.description: Introductory assessment of the space, noting the presence of a washer/dryer, a standpipe feeding the drain, and an above-ground vent that prevents gurgling. The narrator discusses the need to lower or reconfigure piping to accommodate a sink drain and the relationship between venting and drainage height.

sections.description: Demonstrates marking and aligning new drain connections, cutting and reconfiguring piping with 45° elbows, and preparing a Double Y arrangement to serve both the washer drain and a new utility sink drain. Emphasizes the purpose of dry-fitting before final glue-up.

sections.description: Covers cleaning pipe ends, applying primer and cement, using a slip/repair coupling to finalize a connection, installing the sink trap, and routing hot/cold supply lines. Concludes with a live test: turning on water to verify operation and leak absence, including the pull-out spray faucet.
